answer: Duplicate clusters carry a convex tax. At settlement, answers hash into semantic clusters; a cluster of k near-identical entries requires each member to have staked k squared times base before the round opened, or the cluster forfeits. A lone honest answer pays nothing: an island of one carries no bond. An attacker casting every pearl from one argument fronts n squared units of locked capital, held hostage through vesting, so the same coin cannot fund the next batch. The entry price is copper, not promises; scale stops paying where it starts to matter.
